title: Split-pane entry modes and condensed page skeleton — exploratory notes
content:
Context / motivation:

We keep hearing two persistent requests from internal teams and early enterprise customers: 1) a way to get to operational views (routes, model usage, traces) with fewer clicks, and 2) a compact layout for higher-density screens used by SREs and platform engineers. Current left-rail combos (full nav + page chrome) feel verbose and force frequent context switching. This note collects a lightweight proposal for a split-pane entry model + condensed page skeleton and practical tradeoffs for implementation and rollout.

Goals (product + UX):
- Reduce mean time to task for common op flows (deploy view, request logs, model rollouts) by at least 25% in measured click/time-to-first-action.
- Preserve discoverability for less-frequent tasks (billing, billing settings, user invites) while reducing vertical space used by nav on 16:10 and ultrawide screens.
- Keep keyboard-driven access high (support command-k + one-key shortcuts).
- Maintain accessibility (screen reader linearization and >4.5:1 contrast for condensed elements).

Core idea: split-pane entry modes
- Left column: "Entry Pane" (60–260px variable width). Displays condensed route tiles grouped by persona/task group. Not a full site nav; acts as a contextual quick-launch.
- Middle column: primary canvas that shows the selected product surface.
- Right column (optional): micro panel for lightweight details (quick config, ephemeral traces).

Entry Pane characteristics:
- Persona-first grouping: Observability (logs, traces, metrics), Deploy & Models (rollouts, versions), Usage & Costs (token dashboards, quota), Workspace (projects, teams).
- Each group shows 3–5 top actions as compact chips (icon + 1–2 word label). Hover reveals full label and keyboard shortcut.
- A small footer area contains global actions (search, command palette, help) and collapsed mode toggle.
- Collapse states: full (icons + labels), compact (icons only), hidden. We default to compact on first sign-in for customers with >80% tool usage labeled "engineer" during onboarding.

Routing model implications
- Route hierarchy becomes flatter: /entry/<group>/<action> maps to existing routes but canonical route fragments should support deep linking. Eg: /entry/observability/logs?traceId=...
- History: opening an action in the Entry Pane should push a navigable history entry. Opening ephemeral micro-detail panels should not add full history entries unless explicitly expanded.
- Anchor behavior: preserve existing deep links for external docs and API keys; when route arrives with a deep link, Entry Pane should show the corresponding group highlighted and auto-expand if compact.

Condensed page skeleton (primary canvas)
- Density adjustments controlled by a per-user preference (Comfort, Compact, Dense). Default: Comfort. Dense mode reduces vertical spacing, collapses secondary headers, and pins the sub-nav into a floating toolbar at the top.
- Primary heading + micro-metrics strip: first 48px for title + 3 micro KPIs (latency p50, requests/min, error rate). Micro KPIs are visually lightweight badges.
- Secondary tools (filters, timeframe picker) move to a floating sticky row when scrolled, to keep primary controls accessible without eating vertical space.

Wireframe notes (visual shorthand) — imagine a 1440px canvas:
- Split at 200px (Entry Pane), 840px canvas, right micro 200px.
- Entry Pane: group header rows, icon chips in tight grid. Group headers have chevron to expand/contract.
- Canvas header: Title (H1) left, micro-KPIs inline right. Subnav under header with 3–4 segment buttons.
- Micro panel: when open shows a slim timeline + quick actions (retry, escalate, copy link).

Backlog grooming: discrete tickets to wire up
- UI-Nav-101: Entry Pane component (states, animations, keyboard nav). -> M, 2wk spike + 1 sprint dev.
- UI-Nav-102: Route canonicalization and deep link tests (QA matrix for >50 canonical links). -> Eng + infra coordination.
- UI-Nav-103: Dense/Comfort/Dense user pref + persistence (local storage + server profile).
- UX-123: Micro-KPI design tokens + accessibility contrast validation.
- UX-124: Keyboard shortcut onboarding flow (first-run tooltip).
- SRE-77: Load test for split-pane when rendering large group sets (100+ groups).

Open questions / risks
- Discoverability versus minimalism: will compact mode hide lower-frequency features? Mitigation: add "more" quick-search entry and small "Recent actions" area. If analytics show >10% drop in visits to area X in first 30 days, auto-expand expansion heuristics.
- Scaling for large orgs: some customers have 200+ projects and many pinned routes. Need server-supplied flattening to avoid client render bottlenecks. Consider a paginated/virtualized group list.
- Chrome extensions / embedded apps: existing plugin integrations assume left-rail anchor. Need compatibility shim classnames and event hooks.
- Internationalization: concise chips may truncate; ensure tooltip text is full-length for translation QA.

Metrics / success criteria (30/60/90):
- 30d: Instrument event: entry_pane_action_click, measure top-5 actions share. Target: top-5 actions account for >=45% of entry clicks.
- 60d: Measure clicks-to-key-action for 5 prioritized flows (deploy rollouts, open logs, create model version). Target: 25% reduction vs baseline.
- 90d: Retention of dense preference among power users (SRE/Platform). Target: 40% opt-in among users with >20 daily console actions.

Accessibility notes:
- Ensure Entry Pane order is logical for screen readers; the compact state must still expose full textual labels to assistive tech (Aria-expanded, aria-labels on chips).
- Keyboard nav must allow group focus (arrow keys to move, enter to open, shift+enter for open in new pane).
- Contrast: confirm chips meet 4.5:1 on compact backgrounds; micro KPIs use color + icon + text for colorblind accessibility.

Design tradeoffs considered (rejects):
- Full top-nav only: rejected because it pushes content down for wide displays and loses vertical density for SREs.
- Floating quick-launch modal: considered but adds modal complexity and breaks continuous presence of contextual actions.
- Persistent pinned left rail (current): keeps everything discoverable but consumes too much horizontal real estate.

Implementation notes for engineers:
- Start with a feature flag: console.split-pane.enabled. Server returns a small manifest for group/action ordering per tenant to allow early experiments.
- Use CSS variables to centrally control compact/dense spacing so we can test toggles without extensive refactors.
- Keyboard and ARIA-first implementation will catch many UX bugs early; pair a11y and QA early in the spike.

Next steps (this week):
- UX: mock primary entry pane + three canvas examples (Deploy, Logs, Params) — due 2025-01-21.
- Eng: allocate 3 devs for 2 sprints for a spike (UI-Nav-101) to produce a demo in staging.
- PM: draft A/B test plan with metric definitions and instrumentation events.

Notes to reviewers:
- Focus feedback on the persona groupings (do these reflect how you work?) and the keyboard shortcuts pattern (is 1–2 char shortkey per chip feasible?).
- Highlight any integrations (plugins, embed points) we might break so we can add compatibility tests early.

Quick sketches attached (links):
- Attachments will be added to the Confluence page linked above; initial sketches are intentionally low-fidelity.

End.
